scope: Fresh hosted Windows AMD64/ARM64 explicit product DNS restoration after controlled loss of an already working managed DNSCrypt-proxy service; retained DoH/DNSCrypt-proxy ordinary round trips. Fixture-only extension; runtime product bytes unchanged.
serviceLossProcedure: Actual source-built product configures the pinned native DNSCrypt-proxy component and automatic service.
Independent oracle verifies configured DNS families; an ordinary example.com A query with cleared cache/no hosts file/no explicit server succeeds.
Fixture stops only its freshly owned AccessWeaver-dnscrypt service, confirms Stopped and confirms no process remains at the installed component path.
After cache clearing, the same ordinary OS resolver query must fail. The exception remains private; only a fixed boolean is retained.
Actual product dns-restore is invoked; independent oracle compares original DHCP/static modes, ordered static servers, global DoH and dormant state.
The same ordinary OS resolver query succeeds again after restoration.
Actual product removes its managed DNSCrypt service; component identity, removed snapshot and all three joined CLI/capture completions are required.
limitations: These observations prove explicit product recovery after controlled service loss on fresh hosted Windows AMD64/ARM64. They do not prove automatic failover, automatic configuration rollback, spontaneous process crash, real DoH outage, reboot/power-loss recovery or the complete DNS gate.

The DNSCrypt-proxy component can use multiple encrypted protocols. Proxy-path resolution does not independently prove DNSCrypt packet exchange or exclude every plaintext fallback; encrypted transport remains unobserved.
The private oracle compares actual original state. No registry values, DNS original addresses, adapter identities, process IDs, host paths, accounts, exception details or raw logs are exported.
Source fault tests prove coordinator ordering/cleanup/refusal contracts with mocks, not every native failure mechanism.
Native source-built fixtures do not qualify installed/signed packages, all Windows versions, domain/MDM-managed endpoints, real adapter hotplug or every static/link-local configuration.

Prior ten-target compile/normal regression applies through verified identical product bytes; no new normal/sustained browser run is claimed. Original Firefox sustained RSS/WebKit startup-editor failures and fifty-gate/ten-target enterprise scope remain open.
Mac launch diagnostics, private-output architecture selection and signing public identifiers retain their existing holds; BSD public-source mapping completed.
